newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Senate to vote on surcharge in May.
newsitem.headline: Australian Senate to vote on surcharge in May.

text.p: The Australian government said on Thursday it expected the superannuation contribution surcharge legislation to be voted on in the Senate in early May.
"We will be pushing to have it first cab off the rank when we sit for those extra sitting days before the budget (May 13)," a spokesman for Assistant Treasurer Rod Kemp told Reuters.
The Senate has decided to add three days to its May sitting schedule: May 6, 7 and 12.
The second reading of the bill was passed by the Senate late on Wednesday and the spokesman expected the legislation to pass at the third and final reading in May.
"Labor have given a guarantee that they will pass the surcharge because they say that they support it," he said.
The combination of Labor's 28 and the government's 37 votes in the Senate would pass the bill, even if the minor parties combined their 11 votes against the bill.
Another spokesman for Kemp said the surcharge on superannuation was aimed at reducing the concessions available on contributions made by higher income earners.
He said the current 15 percent contributions tax applies to all employer and deducted contributions.

"What the government is doing now is imposing a surcharge of a maximum of 15 percent on certain contributions -- and that is those contributions made by higher income earners -- those earning over A$70,000 a year," he told Reuters.
